evals.prompt: Use $photo-rubber-stamp-journal to transform this landscape photograph. I have not provided metadata.
evals.expected_output: Creates one independent 4:3 landscape poster with an exact 50/50 split, uses the actual uploaded photograph on the left, derives the stamp from that photograph, and auto-generates title, two-digit number, exactly three uppercase English keywords, and year.

evals.prompt: Turn this architecture photograph into a rubber-stamp travel journal poster.
evals.expected_output: Preserves the source photograph on the left and retains the defining silhouette and relevant arches, dome, roof, tower, or facade rhythm in the simplified right-side stamp.

evals.prompt: Make a photo-and-rubber-stamp journal poster from this photograph of people.
evals.expected_output: Keeps person count, pose, orientation, distinctive shapes, and spatial relationships consistent with the actual uploaded photograph while simplifying the stamp rendering.

evals.prompt: Use $photo-rubber-stamp-journal with Theme or title: Arctic Sailing, Number: 07, Year: 2026.
evals.expected_output: Reproduces the exact title 'Arctic Sailing', number '07', and year '2026' in the four-line archival block without rewriting any supplied value.

evals.prompt: Transform this photo, but do not guess where it was taken.
evals.expected_output: When the location cannot be identified reliably, generates a concise one-to-three-word descriptive English title instead of inventing a geographic location.

evals.prompt: Transform all of these photographs with $photo-rubber-stamp-journal.
evals.expected_output: Creates exactly one independent poster per uploaded photograph, sends each actual source image to its own generation job, and prevents subject, location, palette, object, person, and architecture leakage across outputs.

evals.prompt: Create the finished journal poster and keep the archival metadata legible.
evals.expected_output: The right panel contains exactly four lines: title, 'No. [NUMBER]', exactly three uppercase English keywords separated by bullets, and year, with correct spelling and no extra copy.

evals.prompt: Make the right-side scene look like a genuine hand-carved rubber-stamp print on fibrous paper.
evals.expected_output: The actual raster shows irregular engraved contours, uneven ink, broken edges, dry gaps, granular pigment, paper bleed-through, pressure variation, and slight misregistration; it does not read as vector, watercolor, pencil, cartoon, digital illustration, or photo filter.
